questions.text:
A relational database contains two tables Student and Performance as shown below:

The primary key of the Student table is Roll_no. For the Performance table, the columns Roll_no. and Subject_code together from the primary key. Consider the SQL query given below: 
SELECT S.Student_name, sum(P.Marks)
FROM Student S, Performance P
WHERE  P.Marks  >  84
GROUP BY S.Student_name;
The number of rows returned by the above SQL query is _________ .
questions.solution:
There is no join condition, so FROM makes a cross product: every student is paired with every Performance row.

WHERE Marks [latex]\gt[/latex] 84 keeps the 5 performance rows with marks 86, 95, 90, 89, 92, and each is paired with all 5 students.

GROUP BY Student_name gives one row per student name [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 rows.

Answer: 5

Answer: 5

b points to a[4] = 10. Each step adds [latex](*b-i)-*(b-i)=(10-i)-a[4-i][/latex]:
- i = 0: 10 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 0
- i = 1: 9 [latex]-[/latex] 8 = 1
- i = 2: 8 [latex]-[/latex] 6 = 2
- i = 3: 7 [latex]-[/latex] 4 = 3
- i = 4: 6 [latex]-[/latex] 2 = 4

sum = 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10

Answer: 10

questions.text: In an RSA cryptosystem, the value of the public modulus parameter n is 3007. If it is also is known that [latex]\phi(n)=2880[/latex], where [latex]\phi()[/latex] denotes Euler's Totient Function, then the prime factors of n which is greater than 50 is _________ .
questions.solution:
n = pq and [latex]\phi(n)=(p-1)(q-1)=n-(p+q)+1[/latex].
So [latex]p+q=3007-2880+1=128[/latex] and [latex]pq=3007[/latex].

p, q are roots of [latex]t^2-128t+3007=0[/latex]: [latex]t=\frac{128\pm\sqrt{16384-12028}}{2}=\frac{128\pm66}{2}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 97 and 31.

Answer: 97

questions.text:
Consider the following relation P(X, Y, Z), Q(X, Y, T) and R(Y, V):

How many tuples will be returned by the following relational algebra query?

Answer:______
questions.solution:
Left part: R tuples with V = V2 are (Y3, V2) and (Y2, V2). P has Y = Y2 only in (X2, Y2, Z2) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {X2}.
Right part: Q tuples with T [latex]\gt[/latex] 2 are (X1, Y2, 5) and (X1, Y1, 6); both Y2 and Y1 exist in R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {X1}.

{X2} [latex]-[/latex] {X1} = {X2} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1 tuple.

Answer: 1
